originalTitle: Utah wildfire blocks rescuers from reaching firefighting helicopter crash site
summary: Fate of two passengers onboard helicopter that went down Friday morning remains unknown after more than 24 hours
content: The fate of two passengers onboard a firefighting helicopter that crashed Friday morning in Utah remains unknown after more than 24 hours, as one of the country’s largest wildfires continues to grow, preventing authorities from safely reaching the accident site. The Sikorsky S-64 helicopter, contracted by the US Forest Service, was responding on Friday to the Widemouth 2 fire, a blaze sparked in late July by lightning, when it crashed in a remote area of central Utah. Widemouth 2 has swept through more than 114,600 acres (46,400 hectares) and is 24% contained, as of Saturday. That figure marked a jump from early on Friday, where the fire’s scope was reported as reaching more than 105,000 acres, according to state data. The chopper’s crash ignited a new blaze, state authorities said at a news conference on Friday evening. The accident site is within the fire’s perimeter. “Ground resources attempted to respond immediately, but access to the scene was compromised by the emergent fire,” the US Forest Service wrote in a Saturday statement. “Without a safety zone, the Incident Management Team determined not to place lives at risk until the area is deemed safe.” Federal officials have advised the public to refrain from speculating on the nature of the crash, as search-and-rescue teams wait for fire conditions to subside to safer levels. In a Saturday daily report, however, the US National Interagency Fire Center, a coalition of state and federal agencies, said the helicopter’s “pilot and one crewmember were fatally injured”. At a Saturday morning briefing, a moment of silence was observed to honor the passengers. The US Forest Service has declined to confirm their status. “There have already been many false reports and rumors, and the victims deserve the highest level of respect and avoidance of speculation,” the agency wrote. Investigators with the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) were en route to Richfield, a city roughly 160 miles (250km) south of Salt Lake City, as of Friday. When they are able to reach the crash site, they will document the scene, before retrieving the aircraft. The western US states have faced a deadly wildfire season. In June, three firefighters died, as they battled a blaze along the Colorado-Utah border. A fourth firefighter later died from burn injuries sustained during the emergency response.
chineseTitle: 犹他州野火阻止救援人员到达消防直升机坠毁现场
chineseSummary: 周五早上坠毁的直升机上的两名乘客在超过 24 小时后仍然下落不明
chineseContent: 周五早上在犹他州坠毁的一架消防直升机上的两名乘客的命运在超过 24 小时后仍然未知，因为该国最大的野火之一仍在继续蔓延，导致当局无法安全到达事故现场。由美国林务局承包的西科斯基 S-64 直升机周五在对威德茅斯 2 号火灾（7 月下旬由闪电引发的火灾）进行救援时，在犹他州中部的偏远地区坠毁。截至周六，Widemouth 2 已横扫超过 114,600 英亩（46,400 公顷）的土地，其中 24% 已得到控制。根据州数据，这一数字较周五早些时候有所增加，据报道，火灾范围已超过 105,000 英亩。州当局在周五晚上的新闻发布会上表示，直升机坠毁引发了新的火灾。事故地点位于火灾范围内。美国林务局在周六的一份声明中写道：“地面资源试图立即做出反应，但紧急火灾影响了进入现场的通道。” “如果没有安全区，事件管理团队决定在该区域被认为安全之前不会将生命置于危险之中。”联邦官员建议公众不要猜测事故的性质，因为搜救队正在等待火势消退到更安全的水平。然而，州和联邦机构联盟美国国家跨机构消防中心在周六的每日报告中表示，直升机的“飞行员和一名机组人员受了致命伤”。在周六早上的新闻发布会上，默哀片刻以向乘客致敬。美国林业局拒绝证实他们的状况。 “已经有很多不实报道和谣言，受害者应该得到最高程度的尊重
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
